ms.promise:
Hydra research and risk assessment.
Hydra based accounting system design and architecture
Customer wallet app UX design and user validation
ms.criteria:
Hydra research and risk assessment will provide indication of any potential limitation of Hydra from both functional and non-functional perspectives. The purpose of the system is to sustain a significant number of users, hence having understanding of number of users / merchants we can sustain using one hydra head is key in modelling any scaling solutions. Other questions to be answered: limits for adding utxos to heads and how to most efficiently query information from the Hydra head.
The accounting system design and architecture document will describe key architectural viewpoints, technologie
ms.report:
We have conducted an analysis and risk assessment of Hydra state and the feasibility of using it for our problem. We have found that in its current state, we can implement the solution with some limitations associated with partial commits not yet being implemented. The impact of respective limitation being non-functional (aka doesn't impact the functionality, but rather the cost efficiency of the solution). The analysis results can be found here:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1lpYT6uzvnfiqZDuPDaXrijjnO_MCDEef8JcLXNB55bs/edit#heading=h.ihuw9mgbl289
Following the analysis we have worked on defining the technical design and architecture of the solution, the document outlining the key viewpoints can be found here:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1b_G03TTuOSsm3Ex0B_aD5MMXu7G9K3Y87cQQQdN0-qE/edit#heading=h.m7lrsogspphb
Finally, we have created the design for the Hydra Pay mobile app. These designs have been used as part of user interviews - we have interviewed three different users and collected feedback that, where appropriate, has been incorporated into the final designs that can be found here:
https://www.figma.com/design/lPtdCSKf7g7Ofql3fiYYfe/App-Design?node-id=24-4332&t=WxTZsuNK9SQIdrjX-1

ms.report:
Customer Wallet App Implementation
Milestone Outputs:
Android and iOS customer native apps.

Evidence of Milestone Completion:
1. Android App:
• Video Demonstration:
 A video showcasing the Android app’s full functionality is available, highlighting key features such as depositing ADA, making payments, and withdrawing funds. This demo showcases a number of advanced features, including:
 - Withdraw Capability: Users can withdraw ADA or USDM, selecting between accounts and currencies in real-time.
 - Wallet Management: The app allows users to choose their accounts, add new ones, and view their real-time USD equivalent balance.
 - Currency and Payment Options: Users can choose who they want to pay and with which currency (ADA or USDM).
 - Amount and QR Code Scanner: The app allows users to input payment amounts and pay through QR codes, providing seamless payment processing.
 - Transaction History: The app displays transaction histories along with detailed breakdowns of each transaction.
 - ADA Staking Screen: A dedicated staking screen is available, allowing users to stake their ADA directly within the app.
 - Currency Exchange: The app supports exchange between ADA and USDM.
 - NFC Payment Screen (in progress): Development is ongoing for NFC contactless payments to be finalized in Milestone 4.
 - User Settings (in progress): Additional user settings are being developed to allow for greater personalization.

ms.report:
This document represents the proof of achievement for Milestone 3 of the Hydra-Enabled Accounting and Micropayments System Catalyst project. 

As part of milestone 1 of the project we have defined the designs of the smart contract and off chain code required for the Hydra based accounting system along with the design for the mobile app that will employ the accounting system and expose the end to end functionality to end users. Following that, in milestone 2, we have delivered the implementation of the mobile application (both Android and IOS). As part of the 3rd milestone we had to deliver the smart contract and the offchain code associated with the implementation of the Hydra based accounting system that will be used by the mobile apps. In this context, the code associated with the implementation can be found here: https://github.com/blazarlabs-io/blazar-hydra/tree/main/src

The video demonstrating the functionality of the system can be found here:
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1SobpP3OK0CqjTmNC_thkbp8eYlbclGTa/view?usp=drive_link

As part of the demo there are a number of transactions occurring on chain, these transactions are referenced in the document below and can be examined as a further confirmation of the transactions demoed in the video:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HklUPawheM1L3WmcYSeSjHqtZLMvToBGazsoziuOjWk/edit?usp=drive_link

During the development process, a number of issues were identified in relation to Hydra as well as to the Lucid framework used for implementing the offchain code. The issues have been reported to relevant parties with some of them being fixed already and some others lined up for being addressed. The list of issues along with relevant details have been documented and can be found here:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1QgUYX3GKQ8YBJM9e30xQ3LhCPlmctb4bBCQyVv7p-Dc/edit?usp=drive_link

ms.promise:
Merchant app.
Audit and security testing report: 
・the smart contract will be audited to ensure compliance with requirements
・the wallet app and the merchant app will be tested for security issues to ensure funds safety
ms.criteria:
Ensure the merchant can initiate a payment from the merchant app and the app adheres to the UX design.
Merchant app integration with NFC Reader
Audit and security testing will be conducted on top of regular qa/testing to ensure smart contracts conformity and web app integrity.
ms.report:
In this milestone we are delivering the last key component of the solution - the merchant app. This app is used by merchants in conjunction with the payment terminal (IoT device) used to capture the NFC payment, the terminal has to be connected to the app to enable triggering payments as well as showing balance / settled funds to the merchant. The video below highlights the process of connecting the terminal to the web app as well as the process of initiating and then receiving a payment: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1P-ThxfwPedxG1Rz8XkYDdScyEvRAAUkm/view?usp=drive_link
The link to the merchant app codebase can be found here: https://github.com/blazarlabs-io/blazar-pay-merchant-app
Despite the project referring to implementing an MVP solution, it was our ambition for the implementation of both the on chain code as well as the backend and frontend technology to be sound and provide the level of confidence needed for an application that manages user funds and facilitates funds transfer between users. In this context, the smart contracts audit and security testing of the overall solution are two important factors to provide that level of confidence while enabling us to complete the project with a solution that is built on a solid technical foundation. 
We have audited the Blazar Pay solution with Entangled Labs (E7D - https://entangled.cardano.vip/), specifically the audit has been conducted by Marius Georgescu, a certified Cardano Solution Architect, with over 5 years of experience in developing on Cardano - https://www.linkedin.com/in/georgescumarius/
The audit report didn’t highlight any major issues or deficiencies - on the contrary it has reinforced that the implementation follows best practices and solid technical patterns.
